subject: Behavioral Economics
title: The Gambler's Fallacy
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Gambler's Fallacy.

hook.text: The roulette ball landed on red six times straight. Gamblers piled onto black. Red hit again.

buildup.text: In 1913 at Monte Carlo, black came up 26 times in a row. Millions were lost betting on red.

discovery.text: The gambler's fallacy: believing past random events influence future ones. Each spin is independent.

twist.text: We see patterns in randomness because brains evolved to find structure, even where none exists.

climax.text: The coin has no memory. The roulette wheel has no memory. Past outcomes don't change future odds.

punchline.text: Randomness doesn't owe you a correction.

quiz.question: What is the gambler's fallacy?
options: Believing past random events affect future ones
Thinking you can always win if you try harder
Betting more money when you're losing
